decisive_items: Six years earlier, she had undergone breast-conserving surgery with endocrine therapy and radiation (50 Gy in 25 fractions) to the left breast for an upper inner quadrant carcinoma.
On examination, there was a 20 mm firm mass fixed to the pectoralis major muscle;
On three-month follow-up, the lesion had increased in size.
response.rationale: The latency, prior radiation field, deep chest-wall-fixed enlarging mass, and nondiagnostic core biopsy best fit a radiation-induced sarcoma rather than simple recurrence, fat necrosis, or primary breast sarcoma.

rejected.why: Local recurrence is possible but is less supported by a chest-wall-fixed deep lesion and a core biopsy showing only atrophic mammary glands.
Fat necrosis can appear as a post-radiation complex mass, but interval enlargement and fixation to the pectoralis muscle make it unlikely.
A primary sarcoma could resemble this mass, but the specific prior irradiation and latency strongly favor a radiation-induced sarcoma.
This repeats the recurrence differential without adding supportive evidence and is contradicted by the nondiagnostic core biopsy.
